newsitem.title: JAPAN: MOF says low interest rates helping Japan economy.
newsitem.headline: MOF says low interest rates helping Japan economy.

text.p: Japan's current low interest rate policy is playing a major role in the economic recovery, Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told a parliamentary committee on Monday.
"It has lessened the burden on corporations' loans and by doing so, has played a major role in the economic recovery," Mitsuzuka told the budget committee of the Lower House.

Although he said he understood that the record-low rates have hurt households which depend on interest rates for their income, Mitsuzuka added that they would benefit the whole population by bringing an improvement in the economy.
Asked whether the government planned to use fresh public funds to help financial institutions resolve their bad loan woes, Mitsuzuka said the government's stance on the issue remained unchanged.

He said the government would stick to its stance that no further public money should be used for bad loans held at non-bank financial institutions other than those at the failed "jusen" mortgage firms.
The government last year budgeted 685 billion yen in tax money to help wind up failed mortgage firms.

The issue of pitching in tax money has recently come into the spotlight again after an opposition politician made a call to reopen debate on the issue, followed by supportive comments by key members of the ruling Liberal Democratic Party.
